body:
if I change  first `where()` to `orWhere()`
```
WHERE 
  (
    (
      Tests.id = 1 
      AND Tests.title = 'test'
    ) 
    OR Tests.id = 2 
    OR Tests.title = 'test' 
    OR Tests.id = 3 
    OR Tests.title = 'test' 
    OR Tests.id = 4 
    OR Tests.title = 'test'
  )
```

I think this behavior is intentional. The documentation for `orWhere()` states

>  It is important to notice that when calling this function, any previous set
> of conditions defined for this query will be treated as a single argument for
> the OR operator. This function will not only operate the most recently defined
> condition, but all the conditions as a whole.

Which results in `orWhere` and `andWhere` being dependent on the conditions previously connected. I'm not comfortable changing this behavior as it will certainly break existing applications.
The behaviour is intentional, and something I regret :(
@lorenzo Should we consider deprecating `orWhere()` & `andWhere()` given their less predictable results? They could re-introduced in 4.1 with a simpler to understand behavior.

So why result of first and second usage of `orWhere()` is defferent ?
This method should return same result 
Or `or ( () and () )...` or linear condition `or .. or.. `  for all calling  this method
@markstory I think that's a good plan
4.0 is when we can remove the deprecated methods. 4.1 is when we can introduce again functions that were removed

`orHaving()` use similar code like `orWhere()` and i think there is same problem on that 
`orHaving()` can be deprecate

`andWhere()` can be remove completely because both of `andWhere()` and `where()` have same behavior 
my suggest is removing  `andWhere()` and `andHaving()`

but for `orWhere()`
my suggest is deprecated that and use `orWhere + s` naming for linear `OR` and just linear `OR` if necessary   
or just by `and` condition by  `orWhere` naming

issue.body:
These methods behave differently based on the last used query method. This results in code that has fragile temporal coupling, and hard to  predict outcomes.

Refs #10845
